Petition under Section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation Award
1.

The present petition has been filed by the petitioners seeking compensation of Rs. 30,00,000/-
from the date of filing of the present claim petition till its realization being legal representatives of deceased Sh. Vishal Singh (unmarried, aged 20 years) on account of death of deceased who died in road traffic accident in question which occurred on 10.04.2015.

The petitioners also prayed for compensation for irreparable monetary loss, mental agony, loss of love and affection and future prospects plus all other heads of compensation as per entitlement, caused due to accidental death of deceased.
MACP No. 4786/16; FIR No. 243/15; PS. Adarsh Nagar DOD: 05.10.2024 2.

The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim petition as averred are that on 10.04.2015, deceased Vishal Singh was sitting as pillion on the motorcycle bearing registration no.
DL4S- BC-5631.

It is averred that while deceased was returning back to his home after meeting his friend Sagar and reached near Kali Mandir, GTK Road, Azadpur Mandi, Delhi, while driving the aforesaid motorcycle at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, driver/R1 took a sharp cut and hit against a truck.

It is further averred that accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of aforesaid motorcycle by respondent no.1, as a result of which deceased fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
Thereafter, driver/R1 and deceased were taken to BJRM Hospital, where deceased was declared brought dead.
Postmortem on the body of deceased was conducted at BJRM Hospital, Jahangir Puri, Delhi.
A case U/s 279/337/304A IPC was registered at PS. Adarsh Nagar vide FIR No. 243/15 with regard to the accident in question.

The petitioners have claimed that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of aforementioned motorcycle which was allegedly being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner.
The offending vehicle i.e. motorcycle bearing registration no. DL4S-BC-5631 was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and was duly insured with respondent no. 3 at the time of accident in question.

3. In their joint written statement, the respondent no.1 & 2 i.e. driver and registered owner have claimed that there is no negligence on the part of driver/respondent no. 1 as he was driving the Dal Bahadur vs Avnish Kumar on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/550554/
2 motorcycle at a MACP No. 4786/16; FIR No. 243/15; PS. Adarsh Nagar DOD: 05.10.2024 normal speed on which deceased was sitting as pillion and the accident was caused by one unknown truck which came from back side and hit the aforesaid motorcycle, as a result of which deceased got expired.
It is further claimed that alleged offending vehicle was insured with respondent no. 3 at the time of accident and insurance company is liable to pay compensation, if any to the petitioners.
It has been further claimed that respondent no. 1 was having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
On the basis of these averments, they have prayed for dismissal of present case.

4. In its written statement, the respondent no. 3 i.e. insurance company claimed that present case is not maintainable as there was no negligence on the part of motorcycle bearing registration no.
DL4S-BC- 5631 as in the present case, IO had already filed the closure report in the concerned Criminal Court.

It has been further claimed that parents of deceased/petitioners had given no objection before the court of Ld. MM on 28.05.2015 that they have no objection if the untrace report be accepted and they are satisfied with the efforts made by the police in the present matter.

Thus,
insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners in the present matter.

However, it has been admitted that offending vehicle i.e. motorcycle bearing registration no.
DL4S-BC-5631 was insured with respondent no. 3 at the time of accident.
On merits, it has denied the averments made in the claim petition and prayed for its dismissal.
MACP No. 4786/16; FIR No. 243/15; PS. Adarsh Nagar DOD: 05.10.2024 5.

From the pleadings of the parties and the documents, following issues were framed vide order dated 21.11.2016:-
1) Whether the deceased Sh. Vishal Singh suffered fatal injuries in road traffic accident on 10.04.2015 at about 10:30 PM at GTK Road near Kali Mandir, Azadpur Mandi, Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS. Adarsh Nagar, due to rashness and negligence on the part of the driver Avinash Kumar/R-1, who was driving motorcycle bearing registration no. DL4S-BC-5631, owned by Sh.
Aman Kumar/R-2 and insured with New India Assurance Co. Ltd./R-3?

OPP.
2) Whether the LRs of deceased are entitled to any compensation if so to what amount and from whom?OPP

. 
3) Relief.

6. To substantiate their claim, petitioners have examined two witnesses i.e. Sh. Dal Bahadur (father of deceased) as PW1 and Sh. Mohit Sharma (alleged eyewitness) and closed their evidence on 23.09.2019.
On the other hand, no evidence was adduced by respondents no. 1 & 2 and their evidence was closed vide order dated 12.09.2022.

Insurance company has examined one witness i.e.
R3W1 Sh. Ajay Sharma, official from the office of insurance company and its evidence was closed vide order dated 03.02.2020.

Dal Bahadur vs Avnish Kumar on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/550554/
3 7.

I have heard arguments advanced at Bar by learned counsel for the L.Rs of deceased/petitioners and learned counsel for insurance MACP No. 4786/16; FIR No. 243/15; PS. Adarsh Nagar DOD:
05.10.2024 company and have gone through the documents filed alongwith the present claim petition.

8. Since this is a claim petition under Section 166 and 140 of Motor Vehicles Act and to be held entitled for the compensation on account of death of Sh. Vishal Singh, the petitioners are required to prove the negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle i.e. motorcycle bearing registration no. DL4S-BC-5631.

The petitioners are seeking compensation with regard to the fatal injuries suffered by Sh. Vishal Singh in the accident occurred on 10.04.2015 near Kali Mandir, GTK Road,
Azadpur Mandi, Delhi, involving motorcycle bearing registration no. DL4S-BC-5631 (alleged offending vehicle) stated to be driven in a rash and negligent manner by respondent no. 1 Sh. Avnish Kumar.

9. In order to prove the negligence of driver of offending vehicle i.e. motorcycle bearing registration no. DL4S-BC-5631, the petitioners have examined Sh. Mohit Sharma, the alleged eyewitness of the accident as PW-2.
He deposed that on 10.04.2015 at about 10.30 PM, deceased Vishal Singh was sitting as pillion on the aforesaid motorcycle.

He further deposed that while returning back to his home after meeting his friend Sagar, when he reached near Kali Mandir, GTK Road, Azadpur Mandi, Delhi, the driver/R1 while driving the aforesaid motorcycle at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, took a sharp cut and hit MACP No. 4786/16; FIR No. 243/15; PS. Adarsh Nagar DOD: 05.10.2024 the motorcycle against a truck.

He further deposed that accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of aforesaid motorcycle by respondent no.1, as a result of which deceased fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
During his cross-examination on behalf of respondents no. 1 & 2
, he deposed that he was on the motorcycle of his friend Vishal bearing registration no. DL 1SX 7945.
He further deposed that they all were returning after meeting with his friend Sagar and were returning to their home.
He further deposed that he was alone on the motorcycle.
He further deposed that Vishal was sitting with Avnish Kumar as per his own wish.
He further deposed that they all were not under the influence of alcohol.
He deposed that speed of his motorcycle was between 40 to 45 kmph, however, the speed of motorcycle of respondent no. 1 was 60 kmph.
He further deposed that respondent no. 1 took a sharp cut from left side and drove his motorcycle in zigzag way.
He further deposed that at the time of accident, respondent no. 1 was at a distance of 200 meters ahead of his motorcycle.
He deposed that there was low traffic on the road and there was only one or two vehicles near and around them.
He deposed that the respondent no. 1 had overtaken the truck from left side and the motorcycle collided with the alleged truck.
He admitted that police recorded his statement.
He denied the suggestion that accident was caused only due to the negligence of alleged truck and not due to the negligence of respondent no. 1.
He further denied the suggestion that accident was not caused to due rash, negligent and speedy driving of respondent no. 1 while driving the motorcycle bearing no. DL4S-BC-5631.

He further denied the suggestion that he was deposing MACP No. 4786/16; FIR No. 243/15; PS. Adarsh Nagar DOD:
05.10.2024 falsely just to give benefit in getting financial benefit from the Insurance Company in accidental claim.
During his cross-examination on behalf of insurance company, he deposed that he did not have any idea regarding the address of Sagar, where he visited on the date of accident.

He further deposed that the distance between the place of occurrence from the residence of Sagar was Dal Bahadur vs Avnish Kumar on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/550554/
4 hardly  km.
He deposed that the vehicle he was driving at the time of accident was belonging to Sagar, though now, he did not remember the registration number of the said vehicle.
He further deposed that though, he had driving licence but he did not own any vehicle.
He further deposed that the speed of the motorcycle at the time of accident was 42-45 kmph.
He further deposed that the motorcycle on which deceased was pillion rider was at the speed of 60 kmph.
He further deposed that the alleged truck was ahead of him.
He admitted that the place where the accident had taken place was a straight road having divider.
He further deposed that the accident had taken place on the left side of the road.
He further deposed that he took the injured to BJRM Hospital in an auto.
He deposed that police had not arrived at the spot in his presence.
He deposed that he had not made any call to the police or ambulance from the spot.
He deposed that he had spoken to the relatives of the deceased just after he was declared dead in hospital.
He further deposed that he remained in BJRM hospital for about 3 hours.
He further deposed that the police officials had reached in BJRM Hospital but they had not asked anything from him.
He deposed that police officials had met him in the hospital but they had not met him later on.

He further deposed that the police officials had recorded his statement after about MACP No. 4786/16; FIR No. 243/15; PS. Adarsh Nagar DOD:
05.10.2024 one month of the accident.

He admitted that in his statement u/s. 161 Cr. P.C. Ex.
PW2/X1, he told the police that the accident had taken place due to the fault of truck.
He volunteered that the accident had also taken place due to the more negligence of motorcycle.
He further admitted that he had made statement to the police that accident had taken place due to high speed of the truck registration number of which he could not record.
He deposed that his statement Ex. PW2/X1 was correct.
10. It is an undisputed fact that FIR No. 243/15 u/s 279/337/304A IPC was registered at PS Adarsh Nagar with regard to accident in question.

Copy of said FIR(Ex. PW1/1) would show that same was registered on the basis of statement of Sh. Avnish (Respondent no. 1 herein) wherein he attributed the entire negligence on the part of driver of unknown truck in causing the accident in question.

The very fact that respondent no. 1 herein is the complainant in criminal case, would show that he was an interested person and thus, it can not be inferred from the contents of FIR in question that it was only the driver of unknown truck due to whose rash and negligent driving, the accident in question had taken place.
11.

The heavy reliance placed by Ld. Counsel for insurance company on the statement u/s 161 Cr. P.C of Sh. Mohit Sharma purportedly recorded in criminal case, can be of great help for deciding this issue as insurance company put the said statement Ex. PW2/X1 to PW2 Sh. Mohit Sharma during his cross-examination, wherein he MACP No. 4786/16; FIR No. 243/15; PS. Adarsh Nagar DOD:
05.10.2024 admitted that he had told the police that the accident had taken place due to fault of truck and that his statement Ex. PW2/X1 is correct.
This is apart from the fact that petitioners themselves accepted the untrace report filed before the court of Ld. MM vide their statement recorded on 28.05.2015.

Claims Tribunal is under an obligation to ascertain independently on the basis of material and the evidence which has been brought on record during the course of enquiry as to whose negligence, the motor vehicular accident took place.
12.

It be noted that PW-2 Sh. Mohit Sharma has admitted in his cross-examination by the insurance company that he had told the police in his statement u/s. 161 Cr. P.C that accident had taken place Dal Bahadur vs Avnish Kumar on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/550554/
5
due to the fault of truck.

As per the said statement, no fault of driver of motorcycle bearing no.
DL4S-BC-5631 has been alleged but in the present case, PW2 deposed that accident took place due to negligence of driver of motorcycle.
This shows contradictory versions given by the said witness.
Hence, he is not a reliable witness.
Moreover, the petitioners had accepted the untrace report in the court of Ld. JMFC/MM without alleging any negligence of the driver of motorcycle.
Hence, in view of the above, petitioners have failed to bring on record any evidence to show the negligence of driver of motorcycle.
DAR filed by IO was also untrace in view of the statement made by the aforesaid witness.
There is no other material on record which shows the rash and negligent driving of the alleged motorcycle bearing no. DL4S-BC-5631 by the respondent no. 1.

The petitioners have not adduced any evidence in rebuttal of final report MACP No. 4786/16; FIR No. 243/15; PS. Adarsh Nagar DOD: 05.10.2024 under Section 173 Cr. PC filed by the investigating officer to the effect that the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of aforesaid motorcycle by respondent no. 1 not by an unknown truck.
The petitioners have also failed to file any protest petition before the concerned court of Ld. MM to the effect that they are not satisfied with the untrace report.

13. Hence, in view of above discussion it is held that the petitioners have failed to prove even on the principles of preponderance of probabilities that the deceased Sh. Vishal Singh, suffered fatal injuries in the accident which occurred on 10.04.2015 near Kali Mandir, GTK Road, Azadpur Mandi,
Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of motorcycle bearing registration no. DL4S-BC-5631 by respondent no. 1 Sh. Avnish Kumar.
Issue no.1 is accordingly decided in favour of respondents and against the petitioners.
ISSUE NO.2 14. In view of findings on issue no.1(supra), it is clear that the petitioners have failed to prove the negligence on the part of driver of motorcycle bearing no. DL4S-BC-5631.

Since, this is a claim petition under Section 166 and 140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the petitioners have failed to prove the negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities, hence they are not entitled to any compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.
MACP No. 4786/16; FIR No. 243/15; PS. Adarsh Nagar DOD: 05.10.2024 15.
In view of findings on issues no.1 and 2 (supra), present claim petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is dismissed.
Copy be given dasti.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
